title: Determining wavelength with a diffraction grating

questions.answer: Direct single-frequency light normally onto a grating of known spacing. Identify the central maximum and a matching pair of the same known order n. Measure the angular separation between the left and right maxima, re-find both maxima and repeat. Calculate the mean separation and halve it to obtain θ. Use λ = d sin θ/n, first converting a ruling density to spacing d in metres if required.
accepted_alternatives: A method may use angular scale readings for the two maxima and subtract them for each separation. Details of spectrometer structure or operation are neither needed nor rewarded.

marking_points.text: Uses single-frequency light incident normally on a grating of known spacing or known ruling density.
Identifies the central maximum and a matching left-right pair of the same known order n.
Measures the angular separation between the matching maxima and repeats with independent re-settings.
Calculates the mean pair separation and halves it to obtain the one-sided angle θ.
Uses λ = d sin θ/n, with d in metres, to determine wavelength.
Calculates the mean pair separation as 50.733...°.
Halves the mean separation to obtain θ = 25.37° or 25.4°.
